messages:
maria: heads up — seeing a sharp p95 east-west latency spike between GPU nodes in rack r58 during the midday batching window (11:28-11:40). p95 jumps to ~420ms, p50 stays ~6ms. impact: request timeouts and a few in-flight batch retries. anyone noticing this in us-west-2?

aj: yup noticed it on cluster gpu-prod-3, same time window. logs show RDMA retransmits ramping and some TX queue drops on hca0. filing ticket now. :face_with_thermometer:

liam: can you paste the ethtool/rdma stats? also is this across racks or intra-rack?

maria: intra-rack between node-58-*. affected nodes all in same ToR. quick outputs:
```
$ sudo ethtool -S ens192 | head -n 10
rx_packets: 1234567
rx_errors: 0
tx_packets: 1234000
tx_errors: 14
rx_dropped: 2

$ ibstat hca0
CA 'mlx5_0:1' on port 1: LinkUp
Port GUID: 0x1234...
Vendor: Mellanox

$ rdma_stat --iface hca0
retransmits: 78
rcv_errors: 0

```

sam: interesting — tx_errors small but retransmits not tiny. could be microbursts where NIC queues bail out. did we just push the batch size up in the last deploy?

maria: yes — config change to batch_size cap raised from 64->128 on the 11:15 deploy.

noa: ops-bot alerted at 11:30 with p95 >200ms for route /generate. link: https://redwood/alerts/ALRT-3982 :rotating_light:

ops-bot: ALRT-3982 created by anomaly-detector — affected hosts: node-58-01..08, severity: medium, correlated with batch_size increase.

liam: quick mitigation: can we rollback the batch_size bump on a subset? or throttle batching on nodes in r58?

aj: rolling config to throttle to 80 on r58 now. will monitor.

maria: thanks. while rolling, I captured a tcpdump slice showing bursts of 64-128 packet bursts then a small pause. suspecting qdisc/backpressure + RDMA coalescing. snippet: 
```
11:29:02.123 IP node58-01 > node58-03: seq 1-1500 ack ... len 1400
11:29:02.123 IP node58-01 > node58-03: seq 1501-3000 ack ... len 1400
11:29:02.124 IP node58-01 > node58-03: retransmission seq 1-1500
```

sam: could also be MTU edgecases — jumbo negotiation drift between firmware versions. any recent HCA firmware changes in that rack?

aj: we upgraded HCA firmware on r58-05 last week (to v45). neighbors still on v43. Ops runbook warned about asymmetric jumbo handling but we didn't see perf issues then.

liam: ok that fits: asymmetric MTU/firmware can cause RX fragment drops that only surface during high throughput microbursts. Check if rx_fragmentation counters tick.

maria: checked rx_frag: +0 for most, but one node shows +16 during the window. also noticed kernel dmesg spam: 
```
mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: AER: Corrected error recovered
```

noa: ticket updated: TCK-1129 — suspected cause: batch_size bump exposing firmware/MTU mismatch -> RDMA retransmits -> NIC queue backpressure -> intra-rack p95 spikes. Priority: P2.

aj: rollback completed at 11:36, throttle applied. p95 back down to ~22ms within two minutes. keeping throttled while we triage.

maria: good. suggested next steps: 1) run uniform HCA firmware across r58, 2) temporarily pin batch_size to 80 cluster-wide for next 48h, 3) add RDMA retransmit alert when rate >10/min/node, 4) run controlled perf test (iperf/ib_write_bw) with different burst patterns.

sam: agrees. also propose adding a qdisc tweak to reduce tx_queue_len and enable fq_codel for ens192 on GPU nodes — might smooth bursts. will open PR for a conservative change.

liam: I'll coordinate firmware rollout with hw team but will only do after a maintenance window. want to be careful — firmware changes caused one weird node reboot last month.

maria: noted. for the short term we'll keep throttled and monitor. thanks all. please add any logs to TCK-1129.

aj: adding perf traces and dmesg slices now. will post link when available.

noa: reminder: this only affected us-west-2 racks r58, r60 unaffected. ops-runbook flagged region-specific ToR firmware mismatch earlier this quarter.

maria: closing loop — rollback + throttle kept production healthy. keeping thread open for firmware/long-term fixes. :thumbsup:
